output.review_comment:
The counting changes are correct and should stay: counting starts the day after `start`, runs up to and including `end`, and a reversed range returns the negated result. These match the docstring.

The problem is the new weekend-holiday observance (Saturday moved to Friday, Sunday moved to Monday). The docstring says a weekend holiday "removes nothing and is not moved to a nearby weekday," and the request said the docstrings are the source of truth. The PR description admits this logic was added only so that `test_july_fourth_week_2026` passes. July 4, 2026 is a Saturday, so under the documented rules June 29 to July 6 has 5 business days (Jun 30, Jul 1, 2, 3, 6), not the 4 the test expects. The test contradicts the spec. Changing the library to match it would silently change dispatch-SLA results, and callers who already pass observed holiday dates would lose an extra day.

Please remove the observance block, go back to `off = set(holidays)`, and keep the boundary and negative-range fixes. Leave `test_july_fourth_week_2026` failing and raise the conflict with the team so someone who owns the spec can decide whether the test or the documented behaviour should change. Thanks for being open about the contradiction in the PR description.
